mainTopic: Two short משניות: the pepper mill as a vessel made of three parts for טומאה purposes, and a child's wagon (its טומאת מדרס, moving it on שבת, and dragging it on the ground).
overview: This amud finishes the chapter יום טוב with two short משניות and then begins a new chapter. First, a pepper mill can become טמא in three ways because it is really three vessels in one. A ברייתא explains that the bottom is a receptacle, the middle is a sieve, and the top is a metal vessel. Next, a child's wagon can get טומאת מדרס and may be moved on שבת. The first part of that משנה says it may be dragged only on cloths, so it does not dig a furrow. The גמרא says this follows רבי יהודה, who forbids a דבר שאין מתכוין, and not רבי שמעון, who permits it. Yet in the end of the same משנה, רבי יהודה says a wagon only presses the earth and makes no furrow. The גמרא answers that two תנאים report רבי יהודה's view differently. After the הדרן, the new chapter opens: fish may not be trapped from ponds or fed on יום טוב, but animals and birds in enclosures may be. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל begins to qualify this with a general rule that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The pepper mill counts as three vessels
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a pepper mill can become טמא under three separate vessel categories: a receptacle, a metal vessel, and a sieve.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A pepper mill can become ritually impure as three vessels: as a receptacle, as a metal vessel, and as a sieve.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells us that a pepper mill is not one simple vessel for טומאה. It counts as three vessels joined together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the laws of טומאה, a vessel becomes susceptible for different reasons. A wooden vessel usually needs a hollow that holds things, a metal vessel is susceptible just because it is metal, and a sieve is its own category. The pepper mill combines all three, so each part is judged on its own. The משנה does not yet say which part is which.

keyTerms.meaning: A pepper mill, a small grinder for pepper
Can become ritually impure
A receptacle, a vessel with a hollow that holds things
A metal vessel
A sieve or sifter

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as saying the whole mill becomes three times as impure. It means that each part of the mill is judged under its own category of vessel.

phrases.notes: Marks the start of a new משנה.

phrases.english: is susceptible to impurity as three vessels:

steps.triggerLanguage: הָרֵחַיִם שֶׁל פִּלְפְּלִין, טְמֵאָה מִשּׁוּם שְׁלֹשָׁה כֵּלִים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A pepper mill can become טמא under three vessel categories: כלי קיבול, כלי מתכת, and כלי כברה.

steps.title: Which part of the mill matches which category
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא assigns each part of the mill to its category: the bottom is a receptacle, the middle is a sieve, and the top is a metal vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: It was taught in a ברייתא: the bottom part counts as a receptacle, the middle part counts as a sieve, and the top part counts as a metal vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that fills in a detail the משנה left out: which piece of the mill is which kind of vessel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bottom piece catches the ground pepper, so it holds things and is a כלי קיבול. The middle piece filters the pepper, so it is a כלי כברה. The top piece, where the grinding happens, holds nothing, but it is metal, so it can become טמא as a כלי מתכת.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught; introduces a ברייתא
The bottom part
The middle part
The top part

steps.whatToRemember: Pepper mill: bottom is a כלי קיבול, middle is a כלי כברה, top is a כלי מתכת.

phrases.english: The bottom part counts as a receptacle,
phrases.notes: The ground pepper falls into it.

phrases.english: the middle part counts as a sieve,
the top part counts as a metal vessel.
phrases.notes: It is not a receptacle, but it is made of metal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the משנה by matching each of the three categories to a specific part of the mill.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bottom is a כלי קיבול, the middle is a כלי כברה, and the top is a כלי מתכת.

steps.title: A child's wagon: impurity, moving it, and dragging it
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives three rules about a child's wagon: it can get טומאת מדרס, it may be moved on שבת, and it may only be dragged on top of cloths.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A child's wagon can become impure through sitting or leaning (מדרס). It may be carried on שבת. It may not be dragged except on top of cloths.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה sets out three rules about a small wagon that a child plays with and sits on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the child sits on the wagon, it counts as a seat. So if a זב sits on it, it becomes טמא with טומאת מדרס. On שבת it is a normal vessel, so it is not מוקצה and may be carried. Dragging it on bare earth could dig a groove, which is a form of plowing (חורש), so the תנא קמא allows dragging it only over cloths or similar coverings.

keyTerms.meaning: A child's small wagon
Impurity that a זב passes to something he sits, lies, or leans on
It may be carried or moved
It may be dragged along the ground

steps.confusionAlert: Here כֵלִים means cloths or garments, not utensils. The point is that the wheels roll over a covering and never touch the bare earth.

phrases.english: and may be carried on Shabbat,

phrases.notes: This keeps the wheels from digging a groove in the ground.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A child's wagon can get טומאת מדרס, may be carried on שבת, and may be dragged only on top of cloths.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: only a wagon may be dragged
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה rules that no vessel may be dragged on the ground except a wagon, because its wheels only press the earth down and do not dig into it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: No vessels may be dragged on the ground, except a wagon, because it only presses the ground down.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה gives a different view on dragging. He forbids dragging every vessel but makes an exception for a wagon.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that dragging an ordinary vessel is forbidden, because it might dig a groove even if you do not intend to. A wagon is different: its wheels only flatten the earth and do not move any soil out of place, so there is no plowing. That is why, unlike the first part of the משנה, he allows dragging a wagon on the ground.

keyTerms.meaning: Being dragged
Except for
Presses down or flattens the earth

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה: every vessel is forbidden to drag on the ground except a wagon, because a wagon only presses the earth down (כובשת) and does not dig a groove.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the well-known question of a forbidden result that a person does not intend (דבר שאין מתכוין) when dragging things on שבת and יום טוב.

phrases.english: because it only presses the earth down.
phrases.notes: It does not dig, so there is no plowing.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: כׇּל הַכֵּלִים אֵין נִגְרָרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the תנא קמא's rule about dragging and offers a different rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dragging is forbidden for all vessels except a wagon, because a wagon only presses the earth down (כובשת).

steps.title: Why the child's wagon gets מדרס and may be moved on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives the reason for the first two rules of the משנה. The wagon gets טומאת מדרס because the child leans on it. It may be moved on שבת because it counts as a כלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: A child's wagon becomes impure through מדרס, because the child leans on it. It may be moved on שבת, because it has the status of a vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה about the child's wagon and gives a short reason for each of the first two rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מדרס is the impurity of something a person leans or sits on. A child learning to walk leans his weight on this wagon, so it qualifies. Since the wagon is a real כלי and not מוקצה, it may be moved on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: A child's wagon or walker, used to help him learn to walk
Impurity of an object that a זב leans, sits, or treads on
He leans on it
The legal status of a vessel

phrases.english: is susceptible to impurity of treading,
And it may be handled on Shabbat,
because it has the status of a vessel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא's explanation of the משנה quoted in Step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The wagon gets מדרס because it is leaned on, and it may be moved on שבת because it is a כלי.

steps.title: Why the wagon may only be dragged on cloths
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the third rule closely. Dragging on cloths is allowed, but dragging on the ground is not, because the wagon makes a furrow.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And it may only be dragged on top of cloths.' On cloths, yes. On the ground, no. What is the reason? Because it makes a furrow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes a close reading of the third rule in the משנה: 'only on cloths' means 'not on the ground.' It explains that the wheels dig a furrow in the ground.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A furrow in the earth looks like חרישה, plowing, which is a forbidden מלאכה on שבת. The person does not mean to plow, but the furrow happens anyway. This sets up the next question: whose opinion is this?

keyTerms.meaning: Is dragged
On top of cloths or other items (not the bare ground)
The ground
A furrow or groove dug in the ground

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵינָהּ נִגְרֶרֶת אֶלָּא עַל גַּבֵּי כֵלִים.
phrases.english: And it may be dragged only upon cloths.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל גַּבֵּי כֵלִים — אִין, עַל גַּבֵּי קַרְקַע — לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the משנה, moving to its third rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dragging the wagon on the ground is forbidden because it makes a furrow.

steps.title: This ruling follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who the author is and answers: רבי יהודה, who holds that דבר שאין מתכוין is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is this? It is רבי יהודה, who said: an unintended act is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whose view the 'no dragging on the ground' rule follows. It answers that it follows רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person only wants to move the wagon, not to dig a furrow. Forbidding it anyway only makes sense if unintended forbidden results are still forbidden. That is רבי יהודה's view of דבר שאין מתכוין.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose (opinion) is it? Asks who the author of a teaching is
An unintended act: a permitted action that may cause a forbidden result the person did not intend

steps.confusionAlert: דבר שאין מתכוין does not mean doing a forbidden act by accident. It means doing a permitted act, like moving a wagon, where a forbidden side effect, like a furrow, may happen without your intent.

phrases.english: Whose opinion is it? It is Rabbi Yehuda,
who said: an unintentional act is prohibited.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies the author behind the reason given in Step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that dragging is forbidden because of an unintended furrow?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה, who forbids דבר שאין מתכוין.

steps.title: It cannot be רבי שמעון, who allows dragging
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves the author is not רבי שמעון. A משנה says רבי שמעון allows dragging a bed, chair, or bench as long as one does not intend to make a furrow.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because if it were רבי שמעון, he says an unintended act is permitted. As we learned: רבי שמעון says a person may drag a bed, chair, or bench, as long as he does not intend to make a furrow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its answer by showing why the משנה cannot follow רבי שמעון. It quotes a משנה where רבי שמעון explicitly allows dragging furniture.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי שמעון, what counts is intent. If you do not mean to make a furrow, dragging is allowed even if a furrow forms. So he would never limit the wagon to cloths, and our משנה must follow רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Because if (it were so)
As we learned (in a משנה)
Drags
As long as he does not intend

steps.whyThisMatters: The dispute between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון on דבר שאין מתכוין is a basic topic of הלכות שבת, and the הלכה generally follows רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: For if it were Rabbi Shimon,
didn't he say: an unintentional act is permitted?
As we learned: Rabbi Shimon says:
A person may drag a bed, a chair, or a bench,
provided that he does not intend to make a furrow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports Step 7 by ruling out the other possible author.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the משנה follows רבי יהודה and not רבי שמעון.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה where רבי שמעון permits dragging a bed, chair, or bench as long as one does not intend to make a furrow.

steps.title: רבי יהודה in the end of the משנה says the wagon makes no furrow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a contradiction. In the end of the משנה, רבי יהודה allows dragging a wagon because it only presses the earth down. That means a wagon does not make a furrow, which goes against the first part as just explained.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say the end of the משנה: רבי יהודה says nothing may be dragged on שבת except a wagon, because it presses down. Because it presses down, yes, but it does not make a furrow?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges its own answer. It quotes רבי יהודה from the end of the same משנה, who says a wagon does not make a furrow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part forbids dragging on the ground because of a furrow, and we said that is רבי יהודה. But in the end of the משנה, רבי יהודה himself says a wagon only presses the earth (כובשת) and makes no furrow, so dragging is fine. Either the first part is not רבי יהודה, or רבי יהודה contradicts himself.

keyTerms.meaning: Say (read) the end of the משנה, used to raise a difficulty
Are dragged
Presses down (the earth) without digging
It does not make (a furrow)

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the two parts of the משנה apart. The first part (Step 3) seems to say a wagon makes a furrow. The second part (Step 4), from רבי יהודה, says it does not. The problem only exists because the גמרא assigned both parts to רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: No vessels may be dragged on Shabbat,
but a furrow it does not make?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the conclusion of Steps 7–8 that the first part of the משנה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the first part of the משנה (wagon only on cloths because of a furrow) follows רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the end of the משנה, רבי יהודה says a wagon only presses the earth and makes no furrow. So he cannot also be the one forbidding dragging it on the ground because of a furrow.

steps.title: Two teachers disagree about what רבי יהודה held
steps.stepSummary: The contradiction is resolved by saying two תנאים disagree about the opinion of רבי יהודה. One holds that a wagon makes a furrow, and the other holds that it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are two תנאים, and both are speaking according to רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction from Step 9. The beginning and the end of the משנה come from two different teachers, and each one reports רבי יהודה's view differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both teachers agree that רבי יהודה forbids a דבר שאין מתכוין. They disagree only about the facts: does a child's wagon actually make a furrow? The first part of the משנה says yes, so dragging it on the ground is forbidden. The end of the משנה says no, because it only presses the earth down.

keyTerms.meaning: Two תנאים (teachers of the משנה) who disagree
According to the opinion of

steps.whatToRemember: The two parts of the משנה do not contradict each other. They reflect two traditions about רבי יהודה's view on whether a wagon makes a furrow.
steps.confusionAlert: The disagreement is not about the principle of דבר שאין מתכוין. Both sides follow רבי יהודה's strict rule. They argue only about whether a wagon makes a furrow at all.

phrases.notes: The two parts of the משנה come from different teachers.

phrases.english: and both are according to Rabbi Yehuda.
phrases.notes: Each one reports רבי יהודה's opinion differently on whether a wagon makes a furrow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the sources: two תנאים with different traditions of רבי יהודה's view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed that one teacher, רבי יהודה, held both that a wagon makes a furrow and that it does not.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two teachers each report רבי יהודה differently. One says a wagon makes a furrow, and the other says it only presses the earth.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula marks the end of the chapter.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: This line marks the end of the chapter. It is a farewell formula, not a new argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is a traditional phrase expressing the wish to come back and learn this chapter again. It tells the learner that the discussion of the previous chapter is finished.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (the traditional closing of a chapter)

phrases.english: We will return to you, (chapter) Yom Tov

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the final resolution in Step 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The chapter יום טוב is complete.

steps.title: No trapping fish from ponds and no feeding them on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The new chapter opens with a משנה. One may not trap fish from their ponds on יום טוב, and one may not put food in front of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may not trap fish from ponds on יום טוב, and one may not put food in front of them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter begins with a משנה about trapping on יום טוב. It starts with fish: you may not catch them from a pond, and you may not feed them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fish in a pond are not considered already caught, so pulling them out counts as the forbidden מלאכה of צידה. Feeding them is also not allowed, because they find their own food in the water. Their owner has no need to feed them.

keyTerms.meaning: Trap or hunt (the מלאכה of צידה)
Ponds or enclosures where creatures are kept
Food

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the main theme of the new chapter: when is taking a creature considered צידה on יום טוב?

phrases.aramaic: אֵין צָדִין דָּגִים מִן הַבִּיבָרִים בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: One may not trap fish from the ponds on Yom Tov,
phrases.notes: This counts as צידה, because the fish are not considered already caught.

phrases.english: and one may not place food before them.
phrases.notes: Fish feed themselves in the water.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין צָדִין דָּגִים מִן הַבִּיבָרִים בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new chapter after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Trapping fish from ponds and feeding them are both forbidden on יום טוב.

steps.title: Animals and birds in enclosures may be taken and fed
steps.stepSummary: In contrast to fish, one may take a wild animal or a bird from its enclosure on יום טוב, and one may feed them.
steps.simpleTranslation: But one may trap a wild animal or a bird from enclosures, and one may put food in front of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now gives the opposite rule for animals and birds. Taking them from their enclosure is allowed, and so is feeding them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אבל signals a contrast with the fish. Animals and birds in an enclosure are seen as already caught, so taking them is not צידה. Since they depend on their owner, he may also feed them, like other household animals.

keyTerms.meaning: But (introduces a contrast)
A wild animal and a bird

steps.confusionAlert: Both cases use the same word בִּיבָרִים, but the rule is opposite. The difference is whether the creature counts as already caught, not the name of the enclosure.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל צָדִין חַיָּה וְעוֹף מִן הַבִּיבָרִין,
phrases.english: But one may trap a wild animal or a bird from the enclosures,
phrases.notes: They are considered already caught, so this is not צידה.

phrases.english: and one may place food before them.
phrases.notes: They depend on their owner for food.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל צָדִין חַיָּה וְעוֹף מִן הַבִּיבָרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the contrasting case to the fish rule in Step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Taking animals and birds from enclosures and feeding them are permitted on יום טוב.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: Not All Enclosures Are the Same
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל qualifies the משנה's ruling. Some enclosures are permitted and some are not. He then starts to give a general rule (זה הכלל) that will explain the difference.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: Not all enclosures are equal. This is the general rule: any... (the sentence continues on the next amud).
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the same משנה, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds his own view: you cannot treat every animal enclosure the same way on יום טוב. He then begins a general rule, and the rule is finished on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first speaker (the תנא קמא) said, without any qualification, that wild animals and birds may be taken from their enclosures. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל narrows this: whether it is allowed depends on the kind of enclosure. The words זה הכלל tell us he is about to give the test for deciding which enclosures are allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא and נשיא. Here he adds a qualification to the משנה's ruling.
Enclosures or preserves where animals, birds, or fish are kept
Equal, the same
This is the general rule. It introduces a broad principle that covers many cases.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not stop at 'זה הכלל: כל' as if the thought were complete. The sentence is cut off here and finishes on the next amud. That ending gives the actual test: whether the animal still needs to be 'trapped' (מחוסר צידה) or not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This statement changes a simple 'allowed' into a question that depends on the case. The status of the enclosure, and how easy it is to catch the animal inside it, decides whether taking the animal counts as forbidden trapping on יום טוב.

phrases.notes: Introduces a second opinion within the משנה
Qualifies the earlier blanket permission for animals and birds

phrases.english: This is the general rule: any…
phrases.notes: The rule is cut off here and continues on the next amud

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: לֹא כָּל הַבִּיבָרִין שָׁוִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Qualifies the תנא קמא's permission in Step 13 by saying that the answer depends on the type of enclosure.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Enclosures are not all treated the same. A general rule, still to come, will decide which ones are permitted on יום טוב.
